sections.title: Basic Concept of Active and Passive Voice
sections.content:
In Active Voice, the subject performs the action. In Passive Voice, the subject receives the action.
Step 1: Identify the object in the sentence.
Step 2: Make the object the new subject.
Step 3: Use the correct form of 'be' + V3 (past participle).
Example: Ram writes a letter. → A letter is written by Ram.

sections.title: Simple Tenses (Present, Past, Future)
sections.content:
1. Present Simple: is/am/are + V3
Ram writes a letter. → A letter is written by Ram.
Step 1: Identify Present Simple (writes).
Step 2: Use is/am/are + V3.

2. Past Simple: was/were + V3
Ram wrote a letter. → A letter was written by Ram.

3. Future Simple: will be + V3
Ram will write a letter. → A letter will be written by Ram.

sections.title: Continuous Tenses
sections.content:
1. Present Continuous: is/am/are being + V3
Ram is writing a letter. → A letter is being written by Ram.

2. Past Continuous: was/were being + V3
Ram was writing a letter. → A letter was being written by Ram.

Note: Future Continuous is generally not used in Passive form.

sections.title: Perfect Tenses
sections.content:
1. Present Perfect: has/have been + V3
Ram has written a letter. → A letter has been written by Ram.

2. Past Perfect: had been + V3
Ram had written a letter. → A letter had been written by Ram.

3. Future Perfect: will have been + V3
Ram will have written a letter. → A letter will have been written by Ram.

sections.title: Modals in Passive Voice
sections.content:
Structure: Modal + be + V3

Example 1: Ram can solve the problem. → The problem can be solved by Ram.
Example 2: You must follow the rules. → The rules must be followed by you.

Step 1: Identify the modal (can, must, may, etc.).
Step 2: Add 'be' after the modal.
Step 3: Use V3.

sections.title: Sentences with Two Objects
sections.content:
Some sentences have a direct and an indirect object.
Example: Ram gave me a book.
Step 1: Identify both objects (me, a book).
Step 2: Make either object the subject.
Option 1: I was given a book by Ram.
Option 2: A book was given to me by Ram.
Both forms are correct.

sections.title: Important Rules
sections.content:
1. Always use V3 in Passive Voice.
2. Do not change the tense.
3. Change pronouns correctly (me → I, him → he).
4. Some tenses like Perfect Continuous are generally not used in Passive.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Using V1 or V2 instead of V3.
2. Forgetting the correct form of 'be'.
3. Changing the tense incorrectly.
4. Incorrect pronoun changes.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Object becomes subject + correct form of 'be' + V3 + by + doer. With modals, use modal + be + V3. Practice helps in mastering voice change.

tricks.title: Find the Object First
tricks.explanation: Always identify the object before changing the voice.
tricks.example: She sings a song. → A song is sung by her.

tricks.title: Always Use V3
tricks.explanation: Passive Voice always requires the past participle (V3).

tricks.title: Present Simple Rule
tricks.example: He plays cricket. → Cricket is played by him.

tricks.title: Past Simple Rule
tricks.example: She cleaned the room. → The room was cleaned by her.

tricks.title: Future Simple Rule
tricks.example: They will finish the work. → The work will be finished by them.

tricks.title: Continuous Tense Rule
tricks.explanation: Use being + V3 with the correct form of 'be'.
tricks.example: He is making tea. → Tea is being made by him.

tricks.title: Perfect Tense Rule
tricks.example: She has completed the work. → The work has been completed by her.

tricks.title: Modal Formula
tricks.example: You must obey the rules. → The rules must be obeyed by you.

tricks.title: Two Object Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Choose the easier object as the new subject.
tricks.example: He gave me money. → I was given money by him.

tricks.title: Pronoun Change Rule
tricks.explanation: Change object pronouns to subject pronouns correctly.
